description: Two-instance coexistence AST gate (the audit's headline composability fix): ONE grid+rule family (grids/cartesian_uniform_1d/rules/central_D2_zero_grad_bc, which transitively pulls the interior stencil and the grid) imported TWICE into one consuming model under distinct namespace prefixes (esm-spec 9.7.7) — meshA (N bound to 8 at the edge, free name dx rebound to meshA_dx) and meshB (N=16, dx -> meshB_dx). Every binding loads problems/two_cartesian_grids_coexist.esm (this case's fixture points at the runtime driver itself, so the exact document that simulates is the one whose lowering is byte-pinned), runs the section-9.6.3 rewrite fixpoint over both equations, the two coordinate-expression ics, and the section-6.6.5 inline-test references, and must emit a byte-identical expanded AST in which: the index sets arrive renamed as meshA.x (size 8) and meshB.x (size 16); each instance's compound match D(D(uA,meshA.x),meshA.x) / D(D(uB,meshB.x),meshB.x) is replaced by its OWN makearray (meshA interior [2,7] with ghost-eliminated faces i=1,i=8; meshB interior [2,15] with faces i=1,i=16); the free name dx survives per-instance as the rebound bare references meshA_dx / meshB_dx (so meshA's body carries 1/(meshA_dx meshA_dx) and meshB's 1/(meshB_dx meshB_dx)); zero apply_expression_template nodes; zero unlowered rewrite-target ops; zero surviving metaparameter names. The section-9.6.1 `where` shape constraint scopes each renamed rule instance to its own axis (uA only on meshA.x fields, uB only on meshB.x), so neither instance collides on the other's field — if it had (first-declared-wins), uB would lower with meshA's 8-cell stencil. The golden is generated by the Julia reference runner only (scripts/regenerate-goldens.sh) and compared bytewise by the other bindings.
